fact: Communications minister Sam George said the government has committed US$250 million to the first phase of a national AI compute centre, within US$270 million for AI infrastructure and an AI fund.

Communications Minister Sam George tasked KNUST experts to lead development of a Twi language model, with other universities to lead models for other Ghanaian languages, as the government decided national language models must be built locally.

KNUST researchers developed SignTalk-Gh, an AI system trained on Ghanaian Sign Language datasets that translates sign to text and audio and back for doctor-patient consultations, funded via the RAIL AI4SD project.

Minister Samuel Nartey George says Cabinet has approved US$250 million for a National AI and Computing Centre, described as a funded programme currently being implemented, to give researchers, start-ups and universities access to high-performance computing.
The Minister's representative reaffirmed the government's commitment to establishing a US$250 million AI Compute Centre, first announced by the President at the launch of the National AI Strategy.

Minister Samuel Nartey George says Ghana is committing US$250 million over the next two years to AI computing infrastructure, intended as a regional hub giving neighbouring countries, universities, researchers and start-ups access to high-performance computing.
The op-ed says President Mahama announced in April 2026 a $250 million investment to build an AI Computing Centre.
Hubtel CEO Alex Bram says the company set up an AI lab in 2023 and developed its own AI models, testing some with other businesses, but lacked data to improve them.
The government plans a national AI compute centre, whose first phase has secured US$250 million in funding, per minister Sam George.

Samani writes that Ghanaian companies and researchers are building diagnostic models domestically on local data, naming MinoHealth in Accra and MorphoAI at the University for Development Studies, with no release stated.

Ghana and the UAE signed a $1bn agreement for an innovation and AI hub at Ningo-Prampram with construction scheduled for 2026, including $180m for an AI Compute Hub to be developed by G42, with the UAE's PCFC financing it (African Business).
